stem: A client's AST and ALT are both substantially elevated above the laboratory reference interval. Which interpretation is most appropriate?

options.A: The pattern can indicate hepatocellular injury and should be interpreted with the clinical context, other liver chemistries, and relevant risk factors.
options.B: The elevations establish isolated kidney dysfunction and make a hepatocellular source unlikely regardless of the remaining laboratory findings.
options.C: The pattern indicates preserved hepatocyte integrity because elevated aminotransferases are expected when liver cells are functioning normally.
options.D: AST and ALT directly measure hepatic synthetic capacity, so the values alone establish impaired liver synthesis or liver failure.

rationale: Current StatPearls/NCBI guidance identifies AST and ALT as markers of hepatocellular injury rather than direct measures of liver function. ALT is more liver-specific, while AST can arise from liver and extrahepatic tissues. The same source distinguishes synthetic-function indicators such as albumin and PT/INR from aminotransferases. Therefore substantially elevated AST and ALT can indicate a hepatocellular-injury pattern but require clinical correlation and interpretation with the rest of the liver chemistry panel. A is correct. B ignores a common hepatic interpretation, C reverses the meaning of enzyme release, and D confuses injury markers with synthetic-capacity measures.
educational_objective: Interpret substantial AST/ALT elevation as a possible hepatocellular-injury pattern that requires clinical correlation rather than as a direct measure of hepatic synthetic function or a disease-specific diagnosis.
source_organization: National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI Bookshelf) / StatPearls
source_version_date: StatPearls 2026 edition; last update June 8, 2026; live NCBI page retrieved 2026-08-26
source_locator: Introduction: AST/ALT are markers of hepatocellular injury; PT/INR and albumin better reflect synthetic performance. Hepatocellular pattern: aminotransferases disproportionately elevated. Hepatocellular Laboratory Examination: AST/ALT released with cell injury; ALT more liver-specific, AST has extrahepatic sources; aminotransferases are injury markers rather than direct measures of hepatic functional capacity.
source_claim_supported: AST and ALT elevations can indicate hepatocellular injury but are injury markers, not direct measures of hepatic synthetic capacity, and require clinical-context interpretation.
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential — review laboratory values and diagnostic results and identify findings requiring follow-up.
correction_summary: Balanced option lengths while preserving the distinction between aminotransferase injury markers and hepatic synthetic-function measures.

audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: PASS — the 2026-updated NCBI source explicitly classifies AST/ALT as hepatocellular injury markers and separates them from albumin/PT-INR synthetic markers.
